📚 Today you learned

Working Blind, Part 2 — Triangulating Conflicting Snapshots

When your primary feed is down, one web snapshot isn't enough — you need to triangulate. Today's SPXC search returned three different numbers for three different dates: $181.77 (Sep 18), a day-range of $176.57-$182.01 (Sep 19), and a fresh 52-week low of $172.56 (Sep 22-23). Individually, any one of these could be stale, mis-cached, or from a different exchange snapshot. Together, they tell a consistent story: a steady grind lower, clearly through your $186.90 stop, for at least a week. That's the actual use of triangulation — not finding "the" number, but confirming a trend robust enough to act on even without a live tick. The failure mode to avoid: anchoring on the single most recent-looking result and ignoring that it disagrees with everything around it.

Also today: Data staleness decay — the older an unverified snapshot, the less it should weigh in your triangulation, even if it's the most "official-looking" source.
